text: At last his son. <break time="0.8s" /> The new chief of the tribe. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to him and asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Is it well with you. <break time="0.8s" /> It is well the old man answered. <break time="0.8s" /> And his son told him. <break time="0.8s" /> That there was wood beside him. <break time="0.8s" /> And that the fire burned bright. <break time="0.8s" /> The son said that the morning was gray. <break time="0.8s" /> And the cold had broken. <break time="0.8s" /> And that it would snow before long. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, even now it is snowing. <break time="0.8s" /> Koskoosh agreed. <break time="0.8s" /> And the son explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That the tribe was hurrying. <break time="0.8s" /> Because their bundles were heavy. <break time="0.8s" /> He added that their stomachs were empty. <break time="0.8s" /> And the trail was long. <break time="0.8s" /> And then he asked once more. <break time="0.8s" /> If all was well. <break time="0.8s" /> It is well said Koskoosh. <break time="0.8s" /> For I am like last years leaf. <break time="0.8s" /> Hanging lightly on its stem. <break time="0.8s" /> And I will fall. <break time="0.8s" /> At the first breath of wind. <break time="0.8s" /> My eyes no longer show me the way. <break time="0.8s" /> My feet are heavy. <break time="0.8s" /> And I am tired. <break time="0.8s" /> He went on. <break time="0.8s" /> The son went away. <break time="0.8s" /> And Koskoosh listened. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the sound of his snowshoes faded. <break time="0.8s" /> And he knew. <break time="0.8s" /> That his son was gone forever. <break time="0.8s" /> It was then that he reached out. <break time="0.8s" /> And touched the small pile of wood. <break time="0.8s" /> That Sit cum to ha had gathered for him. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought that if she had cared more about her grandfather. <break time="0.8s" /> Than about the trail. <break time="0.8s" /> She would have gathered more.
